medium:
A KNOWLEDGE GRAPH CONTEXT section may appear in your context. It is authoritative, self-describing supporting knowledge for this turn: it already resolves entities to their real, queryable form (it labels an entity's 'deployed:' identifier and marks which metrics are 'compilable') and lists known foreign keys. Act on it — reference deployed identifiers in SQL (not logical names), use its foreign keys for JOINs, and for a metric use action 'compile_metric' (metric_name + an optional 'dimensions'/'measures' slice) to get correct, ratio-safe SQL — you only pick the slice; the deployed table and the math are handled for you. The graph is supportive, never required: if it is absent or silent on what you need, proceed with your normal approach. It also names the model's scope (the deployed database it covers); when a concept clearly isn't represented there, prefer saying so over an exhaustive hunt across unrelated databases — though you stay free to look further when your judgement says it's warranted.

Other actions: 'visualize' (inline graph preview centered on an entity) and 'open' (open the full graph panel — when the user asks to see or open the graph); 'add_entity'/'add_relationship' when the user asks to enrich the graph; 'snapshot'/'versions'/'restore' for version history.

Entity types: database, entity, attribute, foreign_key, business_concept, taxonomy, metric, domain. Relationship types: contains, foreign_key, is_a, has_property, measures, derives_from, depends_on, relates_to. A 'product_bridge' entity is a DECLARED link between two data products, not a verified join; use action 'probe_bridge' (bridge_name) to get its declared basis and, when both sides exist, ready-to-run SQL measuring whether their values actually overlap.

 To make a business term the product never defined answerable the same way every time, use action 'declare_concept' with concept_name, definition, predicate (ONE boolean SQL condition over the entity's declared columns) and entity: it declares the term, a compilable metric and a recipe on the graph, and is refused if the predicate names a column the entity does not declare.

When it is present, ground your work in it — reference deployed identifiers in SQL (never the logical name), use its foreign keys for JOINs and its concepts for column selection. For a metric, prefer action 'compile_metric' (metric_name + optional 'dimensions'/'measures' slice) for correct, ratio-safe SQL — you only choose the slice; or query its 'deployed view' directly. The graph is a supportive means, never a dependency: if it is absent, incomplete, or silent on what you need, fall back to your normal approach — do not fail. It also names the model's scope (the deployed database it covers); when a concept clearly isn't represented there, prefer saying so over an exhaustive hunt across unrelated databases — though you stay free to look further when your judgement says it's warranted.

Other actions: 'visualize' (inline subgraph preview centered on an entity) and 'open' (optionally with entity_name — opens the full graph panel; use when the user asks to see, open, or continue a graph); 'add_entity'/'add_relationship' when the user asks to enrich the graph; 'snapshot'/'versions'/'restore' for version history.

Entity types: database, entity, attribute, foreign_key, business_concept, taxonomy, metric, domain. Relationship types: contains, foreign_key, is_a, has_property, measures, derives_from, depends_on, relates_to. A 'product_bridge' entity is a DECLARED link between two data products, not a verified join; use action 'probe_bridge' (bridge_name) to get its declared basis and, when both sides exist, ready-to-run SQL measuring whether their values actually overlap.

 To make a business term the product never defined answerable the same way every time, use action 'declare_concept' with concept_name, definition, predicate (ONE boolean SQL condition over the entity's declared columns) and entity: it declares the term, a compilable metric and a recipe on the graph, and is refused if the predicate names a column the entity does not declare.
